ROLE: Accept one pending peer with accept(), then explicitly establish O_NONBLOCK and FD_CLOEXEC on the returned descriptor with fcntl(), mapping would-block to 0 and never treating an accept error as fatal for the listener.

FUNC.NAME: accept
FUNC.ROLE: take one queued connection from the listener

FUNC.NAME: fcntl
FUNC.ROLE: set O_NONBLOCK and FD_CLOEXEC on the accepted descriptor

VAR.NAME: EINTR
VAR.ROLE: retry the accept after a signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM)

VAR.NAME: EAGAIN
VAR.ROLE: no pending connection: reported as the return value 0

VAR.NAME: EWOULDBLOCK
VAR.ROLE: same meaning as EAGAIN on Linux and also mapped to 0

VAR.NAME: F_SETFL
VAR.ROLE: fcntl command used to add O_NONBLOCK to the peer descriptor

VAR.NAME: F_SETFD
VAR.ROLE: fcntl command used to add FD_CLOEXEC to the peer descriptor

VAR.NAME: O_NONBLOCK
VAR.ROLE: file status flag established explicitly on every accepted descriptor

VAR.NAME: FD_CLOEXEC
VAR.ROLE: descriptor flag established explicitly on every accepted descriptor

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: accept
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int accept(int sockfd, struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t *addrlen)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: a new connected descriptor >= 0, or -1 with errno set (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK when nothing is pending, EINTR when a signal arrived)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the returned descriptor is owned by net_accept until it is stored in *out_fd; the listener descriptor is only borrowed and is never closed or modified
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 is classified by errno: EINTR retries, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK returns 0, any other errno (EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOBUFS, ECONNABORTED, ...) returns -1 and leaves the listener usable

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: fcntl
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: for F_SETFL/F_SETFD the value 0 on success and -1 with errno set on failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed descriptor; the flags are modified on the descriptor that becomes the caller's peer
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: on -1 the descriptor already exists and is connected but has the wrong mode, so net_accept closes it once and reports -1 rather than handing a blocking descriptor to the reactor

LOGIC.INPUT: listener_fd: an open, nonblocking, close-on-exec listening socket. out_fd: writable slot receiving the accepted descriptor on success. No input buffer is involved.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out_fd is NULL return -1 (nothing can be reported and a leaked descriptor must be impossible). 2) Set *out_fd = -1 immediately so a caller that ignores the return value can never use an indeterminate descriptor. 3) If listener_fd < 0 return -1. 4) fd = accept(listener_fd, NULL, NULL); if fd < 0: EINTR -> retry step 4 (a signal must not abort an accept that may have completed); EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK -> return 0 (an earlier accept in the same batch already consumed the readiness notification); any other errno -> return -1 with errno preserved and the listener untouched. 5) Establish the mode explicitly instead of relying on inheritance: r1 = fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, O_NONBLOCK); r2 = fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC). 6) If r1 < 0 or r2 < 0, the peer descriptor exists but would be handed to the reactor in the wrong mode; close(fd) once, set errno to the failed fcntl's errno, return -1. Never return a blocking descriptor: net_read_some/net_write_some calls in the readiness loop must be guaranteed not to block. 7) *out_fd = fd; return 1. The listener is never closed, never re-armed and never modified, so an EMFILE burst leaves it registered for the next batch (scope R11: a per-connection failure never stops the broker).
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 1 with *out_fd set to an owned descriptor that is nonblocking and close-on-exec regardless of the listener's own mode. 0 with *out_fd == -1 when no connection is pending (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK) - not an error. -1 with *out_fd == -1 and errno set for a NULL out_fd, a negative listener_fd, any other accept failure, or a failed fcntl (in which case the half-configured descriptor has already been closed by this call).
INVARIANTS_USED: the accepted descriptor's mode is established explicitly by fcntl and never inherited from the listener
a would-block result is not an error and does not close the listener
EMFILE and friends are per-accept failures that must not stop the accept loop
each accepted descriptor is owned by exactly one session afterwards
a single nonblocking read or write call always returns promptly, so an unread peer cannot stall unrelated peers
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: listener_fd is an open listening socket registered in the event loop; out_fd is NULL or writable.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: On 1 ownership of one open, nonblocking, close-on-exec peer descriptor moved to the caller through *out_fd. On 0 and -1 no descriptor was leaked: either none was created or the half-configured one was closed.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Safe with a single accepting thread; two concurrent accepters would split the queued connections.
